Maya (PM): FYI - new competitor "SwiftLite" announced a cheap deterministic-latency offering. Getting inbound asks. Can we check feasibility and launch risk?

Ravi (Eng): Noted. Early thought: a "lite" serving profile using int8 quant + tighter KV cache eviction could cut cost ~30% for short contexts. Risk: regressions on complex prompts. Rough estimate: 2	6 sprints to harden.

Sara (Design): We'll need explicit UX about the trade-offs. Suggest an "Economy mode" toggle with a clear badge: "lower cost / reduced creativity" and a suggested fallback button to full-quality model.

Ling (Sales): Several pilots asked for this exact thing. They want guaranteed p95 latency and a predictable price for demo days. If we don't respond they might pilot the competitor.

Joel (Prod): We should define crisp launch criteria. My draft acceptance checks:
```
- Latency: p95 <= 400ms for payloads <= 128 tokens
- Quality: average accuracy drop <= 12% on our core eval set
- Cost: per-request infra cost reduced >= 20%
- Telemetry: prompt-set regression alerting enabled
- Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> opt-in GA with fast rollback
```

Maya (PM): Trade choices: (1) Fast-follow: implement lite profile and match price; (2) Differentiate: keep existing tiers and emphasize quality/observability; (3) Hybrid: offer pilots for select customers with strict guardrails. Which is realistic?

Ravi (Eng): (1) is fastest but we'll need perf engineering: batching semantics, cache policies, and quantization QA. (2) protects brand but could lose pipeline. (3) seems doable if Sales can commit pilots and Eng runs a focused 2-week spike.

Sara (Design): Hybrid is best UX-wise. We can ship the toggle + inline copy in a week and iterate based on pilot telemetry. No product page overhaul needed yet.

Ling (Sales): I can commit two pilot customers for a 6-week instrumented trial if we provide deterministic latency and rollback guarantees. They need clear demo scripts.

Joel (Prod): Observability is non-negotiable. We must tie quality regressions to prompt-set alerts and have a runbook with rollback triggers. ops-bot can generate alert templates.

ops-bot: Reminder - include runbook and deploy checklist. Template: /runbooks/deploy-template.md

Maya (PM): Decide: run a 10-day discovery + spike. Owners:
- Eng spike: Ravi (2w)
- UX flows + copy: Sara (1w)
- Rollout + monitoring plan: Joel (1w)
- Pilot commitments: Ling (confirm by EOW)

Maya (PM): Deliverables in 10 days: spike report, one-pager with acceptance criteria, pilot commitments. Hard stop: if spike shows >12% quality loss we pause parity shipping.

Ravi (Eng): I'll stand up a benchmark branch and share cost/latency numbers in 7 days. Will include eval diffs.

Sara (Design): I'll drop Figma mocks for the toggle, tooltip text, and fallback CTA.

Ling (Sales): I'll confirm pilots by Friday and share customer demo scripts.

Joel (Prod): I'll draft rollout steps, metrics, and alert rules for the canary.

Maya (PM): Quick sync set for 11 days. Ping #eng-oncall if infra help required. :thumbsup:

Ravi (Eng): ack

Ling (Sales): ack :rocket:

Sara (Design): ack :white_check_mark:

Joel (Prod): ack
